# iru_blueprint_library_item_assignment (Resource)

Manages one Library Item membership in a classic Blueprint root. Does not create/delete the Blueprint or Library Item. Assignment can apply policies to that Blueprint's devices; detaching can remove policy. Assignment Maps and conditional node placement are not supported because aggregate membership does not prove node placement. Import by blueprint_uuid/library_item_uuid.

This manages only the exact membership pair. It does not create or delete either
parent object. Assigning can deploy policy to the Blueprint's devices; detaching
can remove policy. Use a dedicated empty Blueprint and inactive Library Item for
live acceptance. No live assignment acceptance has yet run for this resource.

Only classic Blueprints are supported. All Assignment Maps, including maps that
appear unconditional, are refused until node-aware membership can be verified.
The flattened Blueprint list does not prove conditional-node placement. Do not
add assignment_node_id or infer a node from an item's presence elsewhere.

Create adopts an already-present exact membership without a POST. Import and
no-op refresh use GET only. Changing either UUID replaces only this membership;
UUID casing alone does not detach/reassign. Destroy uses POST remove-library-item,
not DELETE of the Library Item/Blueprint. A complete list without the captured
UUID proves absence; collection/page errors retain state. Avoid managing the
same pair from multiple Terraform resources or states.

Writes are never replayed automatically. A failed or malformed response can mean
that membership changed; the composite locator is retained after an attempted
create so the pair can be inspected/imported. Verify the remote pair before
another apply or replacement, especially if Terraform marked it tainted.

## Example Usage


```terraform
# Review policy effects before assigning to a Blueprint with enrolled devices.
resource "iru_blueprint_library_item_assignment" "example" {
  blueprint_id    = "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"
  library_item_id = "11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555"
}
```


<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `blueprint_id` (String) Exact existing classic Blueprint UUID. Changing it replaces this membership.
- `library_item_id` (String) Exact existing Library Item UUID. Changing it detaches the old pair and assigns the new pair.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Canonical blueprint_uuid/library_item_uuid composite identity.

## Import

Import an existing classic-root membership by blueprint_uuid/library_item_uuid,
then match both inputs. Names, node IDs and extra path components are rejected.


```shell
terraform import iru_blueprint_library_item_assignment.example aaaaaaaa-bbbb-4ccc-8ddd-eeeeeeeeeeee/11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555
```


The official API reference documents assignment/removal bodies and UUID-array
success responses but currently repeats the assign URL for Remove. Iru's own API
permission UI explicitly identifies POST /blueprints/{blueprint_id}/remove-library-item.
This spelling is not an inferred DELETE route. Local wire/Framework/real Terraform
CLI tests verify behavior against mocks; they do not establish live compatibility.
